en: Test for English Majors 2019.
zh: 2019年英语专业全国统一考试。

en: Grade 8.
zh: 专业八级。

en: Part 1 Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

en: Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节：短讲。

en: In this section, you will hear a mini-lecture.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段短讲。

en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
zh: 这段短讲只播放一遍。

en: While listening to the mini-lecture, please complete the gap-filling task on answer sheet 1 and write no more than 3 words for each gap.
zh: 请边听短讲，边完成答题卡一上的填空任务；每空填写不超过三个词。

en: Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
zh: 请确保填入的词在语法和语义上都恰当。

en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
zh: 你可以用空白纸做笔记。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览填空任务。

en: Now, listen to the mini-lecture.
zh: 现在请听短讲。

en: When it is over, you will be given three minutes to check your work.
zh: 短讲结束后，你将有三分钟检查作答。

en: Body language and mind.
zh: 肢体语言与心智。

en: Good morning everyone.
zh: 大家早上好。

en: In today’s lecture, I’d like to focus on how our body language reveals who we are.
zh: 今天这堂课，我想重点谈谈肢体语言如何揭示我们是怎样的人。

en: We are really fascinated with body language and particularly interested in other people’s body language.
zh: 我们对肢体语言十分着迷，尤其关注别人的肢体语言。

en: You know, we are sometimes interested in an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink or handshake.
zh: 有时，一个尴尬的互动、一个微笑、一道轻蔑的目光，或是一个很不自然的眨眼、握手，都会引起我们的兴趣。

en: So, what kind of body language am I talking about?
zh: 那么，我要谈的是哪种肢体语言呢？

en: I am interested in power dynamics.
zh: 我关注的是权力关系的变化。

en: That is the non-verbal expressions of power and dominance.
zh: 也就是权力和支配地位的非语言表达。

en: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
zh: 那么，权力和支配地位有哪些非语言表达呢？

en: Well, this is what they are: in the animal kingdom, non-verbal expressions of power and dominance are about expanding.
zh: 是这样的：在动物世界里，权力和支配地位的非语言表达，表现为身体向外扩张。

en: So, you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space and you are basically opening up.
zh: 也就是说，你让自己显得高大，伸展身体，占据空间，基本上就是把身体打开。

en: And, and humans do the same thing.
zh: 人类也有同样的表现。

en: So, they do this when they are feeling powerful in the moment.
zh: 当人们在某一刻感觉自己有力量时，就会这样做。

en: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
zh: 这种表现尤其有趣，因为它确实让我们看到，这些表达力量的动作有多么普遍，历史又有多么久远。

en: For example, when athletes cross the finish line and they’ve won, it doesn’t matter if they’ve never seen anyone do it.
zh: 例如，运动员冲过终点、赢得比赛时，哪怕从没见过别人这么做，也一样会做出这种动作。

en: They do this: so, the arms are up in a ‘V’ sign, the chin is slightly lifted.
zh: 他们会这样：双臂向上举成V字，下巴微微抬起。

en: But what do we do when we feel powerless?
zh: 可是，当我们感觉自己没有力量时，又会怎么做呢？

en: We do exactly the opposite.
zh: 我们的做法恰好相反。

en: We close up.
zh: 我们会收拢身体。

en: We make ourselves small.
zh: 让自己显得更小。

en: We don’t want to bump into the person next to us.
zh: 我们不想碰到旁边的人。

en: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
zh: 当强势者和弱势者处在一起时，就会出现这样的情况。

en: So, what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other’s non-verbals.
zh: 因此，在权力关系中，我们往往会用与对方互补的非语言动作来回应。

en: What I mean is, if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller.
zh: 我的意思是，如果有人对我们表现得很强势，我们往往会让自己的身体缩得更小。

en: We don’t mirror them.
zh: 我们不会模仿对方的动作。

en: We do the opposite.
zh: 我们会作出相反的反应。

en: I am watching this behavior in the classroom and guess what I have noticed.
zh: 我一直在课堂上观察这种行为，猜猜我发现了什么。

en: I noticed that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power non-verbals.
zh: 我注意到，MBA学生的表现几乎涵盖了从强势到弱势的全部非语言动作。

en: They get right into the middle of the room before class even starts like they really want to occupy space.
zh: 有些学生在上课前就径直走到教室中央，好像非常想占据空间。

en: When they sit down, they are sort of spread out.
zh: 坐下时，他们的身体也舒展开来。

en: They raise their hands high.
zh: 他们举手也举得很高。

en: You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in, as soon as they, I mean other people come in.
zh: 另一些人进来时，身体却几乎是蜷缩着的；当他们——我是说，那些人——走进教室时，就是这样。

en: You see it, you see it on their faces and their bodies and they sit with their chairs and they make themselves tiny.
zh: 你能从他们的表情和身体姿态看出来；他们坐在椅子上，尽量让自己显得很小。

en: And they will not fully stretch their arms when they raise their hands.
zh: 而且举手时，他们也不会完全伸直手臂。

en: I also notice another interesting thing about this.
zh: 我还注意到了另一个有趣的现象。

en: It seems women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
zh: 女性似乎比男性更容易表现出这种姿态。

en: I mean women are more likely to make themselves small.
zh: 也就是说，女性更容易让自己显得弱小。

en: Women feel chronically less powerful than men.
zh: 女性长期以来感受到的力量往往少于男性。

en: So, this is not surprising.
zh: 因此，这并不让人惊讶。

en: The second question concerns our minds.
zh: 第二个问题涉及我们的心理。

en: We know that our minds change our bodies, but is it also true that our bodies change our minds?
zh: 我们知道，心理会改变身体；但身体也会改变心理，这同样成立吗？

en: And when I say minds in the case of the powerful, what do I mean?
zh: 谈到强势者的“心理”时，我指的是什么呢？

en: I am talking about thoughts and feelings and the sorts of physiological things that make up our thoughts and feelings, and in my case, that’s hormones.
zh: 我说的是思想、感受，以及构成这些思想和感受的各种生理因素；在我的研究中，具体就是激素。

en: I look at hormones.
zh: 我研究激素。

en: So, what do the minds of the powerful versus the powerless look like?
zh: 那么，强势者和弱势者的心理分别是什么样的呢？

en: Powerful people tend to be not surprisingly more assertive and more confident, more optimistic.
zh: 不出所料，强势者往往更果断、更自信，也更乐观。

en: They actually feel that they’re going to win, even at games of chance.
zh: 即使是在靠运气取胜的游戏中，他们也真的觉得自己会赢。

en: They also tend to be able to think more abstractly.
zh: 他们也往往更能进行抽象思考。

en: They take more risks.
zh: 他们更愿意冒险。

en: So, there are a lot of differences between powerful and powerless people.
zh: 因此，强势者与弱势者之间存在许多差异。

en: Physiologically, there are also differences on two key hormones.
zh: 从生理上看，两种关键激素的水平也有所不同。

en: One is dominance hormone and the other is stress hormone.
zh: 一种是支配激素，另一种是压力激素。

en: What we find is that powerful and effective leaders have high dominance hormone and low stress hormone.
zh: 我们发现，强势且高效的领导者，支配激素水平高，压力激素水平低。

en: What does that mean?
zh: 这意味着什么呢？

en: That means power is also about how you react to stress.
zh: 这意味着，力量也体现在你如何应对压力上。

en: Once we did an experiment, we decided to bring people into the lab and run that little experiment.
zh: 有一次，我们做了一项实验，把参与者请到实验室，开展了这个小实验。

en: These people adopted for two minutes either high power poses or low power poses.
zh: 这些人分别保持强势姿势或弱势姿势两分钟。

en: We, for two minutes, say “You need to do this or this”.
zh: 在这两分钟里，我们告诉他们：“你需要这样做，或者那样做。”

en: And we also want them to be feeling power.
zh: 我们也希望他们能切实感受到力量。

en: So after two minutes we will ask them “How powerful do you feel?” on a series of items and then we give them an opportunity to gamble.
zh: 两分钟后，我们通过一组题目询问他们：“你感觉自己有多强大？”随后给他们一个参与赌博的机会。

en: Before and after the experiment we take their samples of saliva for a hormone test.
zh: 实验前后，我们采集他们的唾液样本，检测激素水平。

en: That’s the whole experiment.
zh: 整个实验就是这样。

en: And this is what we have found: risk tolerance which is gambling.
zh: 以下是我们的发现：首先是风险承受度，也就是参与赌博的意愿。

en: What we find is that when you’re in the higher power pose condition, 86% of you will gamble.
zh: 我们发现，保持强势姿势时，有86%的人会选择参与赌博。

en: When you’re in the low power pose condition, it’s down to only 60%, and that’s a pretty significant difference.
zh: 而保持弱势姿势时，这一比例降到了仅60%，这个差异相当显著。

en: Here’s what we find on dominance hormone: from their baseline when they come in,
zh: 在支配激素方面，我们发现：与进入实验室时的基线水平相比，

en: high power people experience about a 20% increase and low power people experience about a 10% decrease.
zh: 强势姿势组大约上升了20%，弱势姿势组则大约下降了10%。

en: So again, two minutes and you get these changes.
zh: 所以，再强调一次，只用两分钟就能产生这些变化。

en: Concerning stress hormone high power people experience about a 25% decrease and the low power people experience about a 15% increase.
zh: 至于压力激素，强势姿势组的水平大约下降了25%，弱势姿势组则大约上升了15%。

en: Once again, two minutes led to these hormonal changes that configure your brain to basically be either assertive, confident or really stress-reactive.
zh: 同样，只用两分钟就产生了这些激素变化，使大脑进入果断、自信，或者对压力高度敏感的状态。

en: And you know feeling sort of shut down and we’ve all had that feeling, right?
zh: 你知道，就是那种有些封闭、退缩的感觉；我们都曾有过，对吧？

en: So, it seems that our non-verbals do govern how we think and feel about ourselves.
zh: 所以，非语言行为似乎确实会影响我们如何看待自己，以及对自己的感受。

en: Also, our bodies change our minds.
zh: 而且，身体会改变心理。

en: So, power-posing for a few minutes really changes your life in meaningful ways.
zh: 因此，做几分钟强势姿势，的确能够以有意义的方式改变生活。

en: When I tell people about this that our bodies change our minds, and our minds can change our behavior,
zh: 当我告诉人们，身体能改变心理，心理能改变行为，

en: and our behavior can change our outcomes, they say to me “I don’t believe that. It feels fake, right?”
zh: 行为又能改变结果时，他们会说：“我不相信。这感觉很假，对吧？”

en: So, I said, “fake it till you make it”.
zh: 所以我说：“先做出那个样子，直到真正做到。”
vocabulary: fake it till you make it

en: I’m going to leave you with this.
zh: 最后，我想留给大家这样一个建议。

en: Before you go into the next stressful evaluative situation, for example, a job interview.
zh: 在下一次进入需要接受评价、又充满压力的场合之前，比如参加求职面试之前，

en: For two minutes, try doing this, in the elevator or at your desk behind closed doors, and say to yourself “That’s what I want to do”.
zh: 试着花两分钟做这些动作，可以在电梯里，也可以在关上门的办公桌前；对自己说：“这就是我要做的。”

en: Configure your brain to do the best in that situation, get your dominance hormone up, and get your stress hormone down.
zh: 让大脑调整到能在那种情境中发挥最佳水平的状态，提高支配激素水平，降低压力激素水平。

en: Don’t leave that situation feeling like “Oh, I didn’t show them who I am”.
zh: 不要离开那个场合时还觉得：“唉，我没能让他们看到真正的我。”

en: Leave that situation feeling like “Oh, I really managed to say who I am and show who I am”.
zh: 离开时，要觉得：“我确实说清了自己是谁，也展示了真正的自己。”

en: To sum up, today we talked about the nonverbal expressions of power and dominance, and the strong effects of the change of behavior.
zh: 总结一下，今天我们谈了权力和支配地位的非语言表达，以及行为变化所带来的强烈影响。

en: I suggest you try power-posing which is simple but will significantly change the outcomes of your life.
zh: 我建议大家试试强势姿势；它很简单，却能显著改变你人生中的结果。

en: OK, next time we are going to discuss the social functions of body language.
zh: 好，下一次我们将讨论肢体语言的社会功能。

en: Now, you have three minutes to check your work.
zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

en: This is the end of Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节短讲到此结束。
